properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 8 at 1:54AM EDT until October 10 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Duval County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 PM EDT
Saturday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Saturday
night.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Kauai, HI
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 7 at 7:38PM HST until October 7 at 9:45PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The island of Kauai in Kauai County...

* WHEN...Until 945 PM HST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding on roads, poor drainage areas, and in
streams.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 732 PM HST, Doppler radar indicated bands of moderate to
locally heavy rain over Kauai. The heaviest rainfall has been
occurring over southern coast of Kauai with rates of 0.5 to 1
inch per hour under the heavier bands. Minor flooding is ongoing
or expected to begin shortly in the advisory area. Additional
bands of heavy rain with increased rain rates will be possible
over the next several hours.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Lihue, Kapaa, Kalaheo, Kekaha, Lawai, Omao, Kokee State Park and
Poipu.
properties.instruction:
Stay away from streams, drainage ditches and low lying areas prone to
flooding.

A Flood Watch is also in effect for Kauai through Thursday afternoon.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 8 at 1:34AM EDT until October 9 at 12:00AM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of west central Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Citrus, Coastal Hernando, Coastal Hillsborough,
Coastal Manatee, Coastal Pasco, Inland Citrus, Inland Hernando,
Inland Hillsborough, Inland Manatee, Inland Pasco, Pinellas and
Sumter.

* WHEN...From 5 AM EDT early this morning through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A frontal boundary across the central Florida peninsula will lift
slowly north today.  Deep tropical moisture remains over the
region.  Numerous to widespread showers and scattered
thunderstorms are expected throughout the day with locally heavy
rain likely.  Rainfall totals of 1 to 3 inches with locally 5+
inches will be possible.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued October 7 at 10:15PM PDT until October 8 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Hot conditions with maximum temperatures in the mid-90s to
near 105. Mild minimum temperatures and weak onshore flow will
limit overnight relief.

* WHERE...The East Bay and San Francisco Bay Shoreline, North Bay
Interior Mountains and Valleys, The Santa Clara Valley and Eastern
Hills, The Santa Cruz Mountains, Interior Monterey County and the
Santa Lucia Range, Most of San Benito County and the Cholame Hills
in Southeast Monterey County, and Southern Salinas Valley/Arroyo
Seco and Lake San Antonio.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...This level of heat affects anyone without effective
cooling and/or adequate hydration. Impacts likely in some health
systems, heat-sensitive industries and infrastructure.
properties.instruction:
Hydration is a critical piece to surviving the heat. Drink water, and
if possible, take water to those who are vulnerable.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to the early
morning or evening. Take action when you experience symptoms of heat
exhaustion and/or heat stroke.

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 7 at 9:31PM PDT until October 9 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, surf of 3 to 6 feet
and dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, minor coastal flooding around high tides expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 PM PDT Tuesday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of beach parking lots, boardwalks, and roads
with only isolated road closures expected. Minor coastal erosion
is also expected. Additionally, elevated surf will lead to
strong rip currents and dangerous swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides are expected to peak between
6.5 and 7.0 feet during the mornings and evenings.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.
